metadata.case_name: LAU KA PO (A MINOR) v. MAN CHEUK MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: Kitchen assistant / various low-skilled kitchen jobs (restaurant and canteen)

injuries.description: Brain injury / head injury (with cerebral oedema/post-traumatic brain damage)
source: The major injury in this case is one of brain damage.
brain injuries resulting in personality change and cognitive impairment.
diagnosis by the Princess Margaret Hospital was one of post-traumatic epilepsy ("PTE").
I further find the grand mal epilepsy suffered by the Plaintiff was a direct consequence of the head injury.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

source: X-ray showed undisplaced fracture of right fibula and it was treated conservatively.

injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head
Abrasion of other or unspecified sites of head
Contusion of other or unspecified parts of lower leg

manifestations.description: Occasional occipital headaches occurring on an average once every two weeks lasting as long as 3 or 4 hours
Very poor memory; misplaces objects; has difficulty in recalling instructions
Poor academic performance in school; difficulty in concentration
Personality change: has become dull and easily irritable; catastrophic emotional response and poor impulse control; labile emotions and temper tantrums
Has no sense of directions; may lose his way when going to school
Left hemiparesis assessed at 4/5 during admission
Drowsy for 4 days; fluctuation in conscious level; post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) of at least 5 days
Grand mal epileptic seizure (March 1996) and history of similar events; EEG abnormal slow wave present at the right posterior region
Post-Concussional Syndrome: headaches, giddiness, impaired concentration and emotional disturbance (described by expert)

treatments_received: conservative treatment for undisplaced right fibula fracture
treatments_future: psychiatric treatment (judge awarded 3 sessions per year at $1,500 per session)
epilepsy follow-up/consultation (recommendation for three-monthly review by Dr Shroff)

losses.description: Personality change including catastrophic emotional response, poor impulse control, labile emotions and temper tantrums
Left with jobs that involve simple repetitive manual tasks that do not require concentration, good memory, complicated interaction or problem solving

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Deterioration in IQ and academic performance; would probably not have completed education to expected level (Form 5) but for the cognitive impairment

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Pui Ki v. Leung On & KMB
comparable_cases.injury_description: Awards for categories: Serious injury $400,000 - $540,000; Substantial injury $540,000 - $660,000; Gross disability $660,000 - $1,000,000; Disaster $1,000,000 upwards
